claims.statement: @forceorg/ui-theme (packages/ui-theme) is the monorepo's only shared UI package and owns faction appearance end to end: a five-channel palette registry, a chapter SVG insignia registry, and ThemeProvider which maps a theme key onto CSS custom properties; apps/web is its only consumer, importing everything from a flat barrel with main/types pointing at src rather than dist.

apps/web consumes @forceorg/ui-theme source-first: apps/web/tsconfig.json maps the specifier to packages/ui-theme/src and next.config.js lists the package in transpilePackages, so palette and heraldry data edits take effect on the next web build without running the package's own tsc build.

ThemeProvider.tsx carries a 'use client' directive and react/react-dom are peer dependencies, making the package React-coupled and unusable from apps/api or apps/sync-worker; ChapterIcon.tsx declares no directive of its own.

The FactionPalette contract declared in @forceorg/types is key/name plus five colour channels primary, secondary, trim, detail, glow; key is simultaneously the registry lookup key, the value persisted on the army row and the themeKey passed to ThemeProvider, name is display-only, and no code validates colour format or contrast. Source comments still call it the 4-channel Dawn of War system despite five colour fields.

The palette registry is three hand-maintained arrays (13 Adeptus Astartes chapters, 14 Chaos factions including four chaos_daemons_* entries, 29 Xenos subfactions with namespace-prefixed keys such as necrons_szarekhan and tau_tau_sept) spread into ALL_FACTION_PALETTES, and it is subfaction keys, not faction ids, that select palettes; CreateArmyModal re-declares those keys by hand as subfactions[].key/defaultTheme.

getFactionPalette never throws: an unknown key silently returns SPACE_MARINE_PALETTES[0] (Ultramarines), which is the stack's only defence against an unvalidated factionThemeOverride value stored in the database.

paletteToCSSVars emits ten custom properties per palette: the five --c-* channels verbatim, --surface-header as a derived 135deg primary-to-secondary gradient, --surface-card reusing the secondary channel, --surface-border as the trim hex with a hard-coded '33' alpha suffix, and fixed non-palette --text-primary/--text-secondary values, so text colour is palette-independent and no light mode exists.

Pages theme through CSS custom properties rather than the palette object: globals.css styles headings, borders, focus outline and progress bars with var(--c-trim)/var(--c-glow), and CompositeUnitCard.module.css uses fallback-bearing references such as var(--c-trim, #c89d3c) and var(--surface-header, linear-gradient(...)) so the card still renders Ultramarines outside a provider.

The detail channel is effectively decorative: --c-detail is injected and declared in globals.css but never read via var() by any stylesheet, reaching the screen only as a literal swatch stripe inside FactionSelector.

ThemeProvider supports both control modes but derives themeKey as controlledThemeKey ?? internalThemeKey, so when a themeKey prop is supplied the context's setTheme becomes inert; every apps/web route uses controlled mode with its own useState('ultramarines'), making each page the authoritative theme owner.

useTheme() throws 'useTheme must be used within a <ThemeProvider>' when no provider is present — the package's only hard failure — yet has zero call sites in apps/web, because pages read colours through CSS and FactionSelector bypasses the context by importing ALL_FACTION_PALETTES directly.

ThemeProvider theming works purely through CSS custom-property inheritance from an inline style on a wrapper div (style={cssVars}) that adds no class or layout constraint; everything inside resolves var(--c-*) against the palette and everything outside falls back to :root.

The data-faction-theme attribute is emitted by ThemeProvider but selected nowhere: no stylesheet in the monorepo keys off [data-faction-theme] or any per-faction attribute selector, so it currently serves as an inspection/debug hook and as the extension point for future faction-specific layout rules.

globals.css :root hard-codes the same Ultramarines values ThemeProvider would inject and is imported by the root layout, so markup rendered outside any provider is visually identical to an Ultramarines-themed subtree and pages render correctly before a roster fetch resolves.

CHAPTER_PATHS declares exactly the 13 Adeptus Astartes chapters that also have palettes, typed by @forceorg/types' ChapterPathDefinition {name, viewBox, paths[{d, fill?, opacity?}]}; all badges share viewBox '0 0 100 100', multi-subpath badges use separate paths[] entries, and no registry entry currently sets per-path fill or opacity so every path inherits the component colour.

ChapterIcon resolves its key as (chapterKey || chapter) with no normalisation and returns null for an unknown key with no placeholder or warning; since the registry covers only 13 chapters, most Chaos and Xenos theme keys render no badge, which FactionSelector guards with `palette.key in CHAPTER_PATHS` but page headers passing chapterKey={activeTheme} do not.

ChapterKey provides no compile-time safety: it is keyof typeof CHAPTER_PATHS, and because CHAPTER_PATHS is annotated Record<string, ChapterPathDefinition> the alias collapses to string, so nonexistent keys compile everywhere and fail only as a silent null render.

ChapterIcon renders an accessible svg with role="img" and aria-label '{name} Chapter Insignia', class 'chapter-icon chapter-icon--{chapter}', width/height from size (default 24) and fill from color (default currentColor).

isWatermark switches ChapterIcon to parent-relative decoration: width/height are omitted and the icon is absolutely positioned at right -5% / bottom -10%, sized 70% x 70%, z-index 0, pointer-events none, with opacity var(--badge-watermark-opacity, 0.06); CompositeUnitCard relies on this plus its own position:relative and .cardContent z-index:1 to bleed the badge behind each unit card.

The theme selection for a force is UserArmy.factionThemeOverride, a nullable VarChar(50) free-text palette key with no theme table, no foreign key and no validation against ALL_FACTION_PALETTES; POST/PUT /api/rosters forward req.body.factionThemeOverride straight to Prisma.

On load each army route fetches its roster and seeds local theme state from factionThemeOverride when present (console and edit routes both setActiveTheme from the fetched roster, falling back to a synthetic Ultramarines army when the fetch rejects), then passes that state as the controlled themeKey.

Only /army/[id]/edit persists a palette switch: handleThemeChange sets state and immediately calls performSave, writing factionThemeOverride: activeTheme outside the 1200 ms roster debounce. The console, catalog, changelog and dashboard routes hand setActiveTheme to FactionSelector and persist nothing, making those switches per-session preferences.

The offline/guest roster layer keeps theme optional: createRoster stores factionThemeOverride ?? null and updateRoster only overwrites it when the field is supplied, so locally mirrored armies can legitimately have no theme key at all.
The armies dashboard resolves theme per card as army.factionThemeOverride || activeTheme, so armies with no stored theme inherit the page's currently selected palette for their badge.

packages/ui-theme/src/styles/tokens.css and src/styles/composite-unit-card.css are complete, coherent stylesheets that are neither exported from index.ts nor imported anywhere in the monorepo; the effective token source is apps/web/src/app/globals.css and the effective card styling is CompositeUnitCard.module.css, which separately restate the same tokens, so editing tokens.css changes no screen.

Adding or retuning a faction requires only editing palettes/factions.ts (plus chapters/paths.ts for a badge) because FactionSelector, its swatch preview and every themed page enumerate ALL_FACTION_PALETTES; the exception is CreateArmyModal's hard-coded FACTIONS list, whose subfactions/defaultTheme strings must match palette keys manually or the palette is unselectable at creation time.
